name: Huang Yimeng
current_role: Founder, Chairman of the Board and CEO, XD Inc. (HKEX: 2400), Shanghai
profile: Huang Yimeng ('Dash' Huang) co-founded the P2P resource site VeryCD in 2003, then pivoted to games, chairing X.D. Network since 2011. XD (Hong Kong-listed since 2019) runs game development/publishing and TapTap, an ad-supported game download platform that bypasses Chinese app-store revenue cuts. He holds a large stake and still runs the company.
interesting_fact: XD's TapTap is ad-supported and free for players and publishers; Huang publicly argued (Bloomberg, 2021) that hardware makers' 50% app-store cuts should be viewed from an anti-monopoly standpoint, and his stake passed $1bn when XD shares jumped after the Huawei-Tencent app-store spat.
deep_cut_fact: XD's origin is VeryCD, a P2P resource-sharing website Huang founded with Kros Dai (Dai Yunjie, now XD President) in 2003; the same duo still lead XD more than two decades later.
notes: Known in Chinese internet circles as 'Dash'. Company IR email is best route; no personal verified accounts found.

name: Rebecca Taub
current_role: Founder; Board Director and Senior Scientific & Medical Advisor (since April 2025), Madrigal Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: MDGL)
profile: Physician-scientist Rebecca 'Becky' Taub, M.D., taught genetics and medicine at the University of Pennsylvania, then led R&D at Bristol Myers Squibb and Roche (VP metabolic diseases) before co-founding Madrigal in 2011. As CEO, then CMO/President of R&D, she led development of Rezdiffra (resmetirom). In 2025 she stepped back to an advisor role and remains on the board.
interesting_fact: Under her leadership Madrigal developed Rezdiffra (resmetirom), the first FDA-approved medicine for MASH (fatty-liver disease with fibrosis); the company grew from fewer than 10 R&D staff in Conshohocken, PA to 500+ employees.
deep_cut_fact: At the University of Pennsylvania, where she taught genetics and medicine, she was one of the youngest women at that time to become a fully tenured professor.
notes: Wealth stems from MDGL stock. Goes by 'Becky'. Also reported as Industry Co-Chair of the Liver Forum (UC Berkeley) and a BriaCell Therapeutics director (unverified here). Route via Madrigal media team.

name: Zhao Guiqin
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Runben Biotechnology Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603193), Guangzhou
profile: Guangzhou entrepreneur born in the 1970s who started Runben's predecessor, Xinxiang Trading, in 2006 as an OEM/white-label maker, then launched the Runben brand in 2010. Runben grew into a leading Chinese mosquito-repellent and baby-care brand sold mainly online, listing on the Shanghai main board in October 2023; he and his co-founder wife control most of the shares.
interesting_fact: Runben became the A-share market's 'first mosquito-repellent stock'; by 2022 it held ~16% of China's electric mosquito-liquid market and its baby-care line overtook repellents as its largest business. Hillhouse-linked JNRY VIII invested in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: When he launched the Runben own-brand in 2010, he opened a Tmall flagship direct store at the same time, betting on e-commerce years before rivals; Tmall, JD and Douyin later produced ~70% of sales.
notes: Described by 36Kr as very low-profile, rarely gives media interviews. Board office (security@runben.com) is the published channel.

name: Zou Xiaowu
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Click Tech / Easy Click (易点天下, SZSE: 301171), Xi'an
profile: Born 1987, Zou Xiaowu began doing online traffic monetisation as a student in 2008 and founded Easy Click (Yeahmobi) in 2011, pivoting early in 2012 from PC to mobile advertising. The company became a major overseas-marketing partner for Chinese apps and games going global (Cheetah Mobile, Kunlun, Baidu) and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2022; it has since applied for a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: Easy Click's user-acquisition work for Cheetah Mobile brought it up to hundreds of thousands of users a day; at Cheetah's 2014 NYSE listing ceremony, CEO Fu Sheng publicly thanked Easy Click. Cheetah and Lei Jun later invested.
deep_cut_fact: In a sophomore-year wealth class asked to imagine his salary a year after graduating, he wrote 10 million yuan in his palm. His first online income came from a detailed guide to US car-insurers, earning $13 per referral lead; one article made about $10,000.
notes: Studied logistics; taught himself programming. General manager of the listed company is Wu Ying; Zou re-elected chairman of the 5th board (2026 filing). Company formerly branded Yeahmobi.

name: Qi Xinghua
current_role: Chairman (as of latest filings found) and co-controlling shareholder, Zhejiang Cayi Vacuum Container / Jiayi Insulation Technology (嘉益股份, SZSE: 301004)
profile: Qi Xinghua is chairman and, with Chen Shuguang, the actual controller of Zhejiang Jiayi (Cayi) Insulation Technology, a Zhejiang maker of stainless-steel vacuum-insulated drinkware and food containers founded in 2004 and listed in Shenzhen in 2021. The family wealth comes from their combined stake (~65% directly and via holding vehicles).
interesting_fact: Cayi is a specialist OEM/ODM manufacturer of stainless-steel vacuum-insulated tumblers, bottles and food jars, a product category whose overseas demand boom lifted the company's valuation and put Qi on the Hurun China list in 2025.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or bio found. Wealth shared with co-controller Chen Shuguang (shareholder listing). Chairmanship confirmed in a 2021 board notice (https://epaper.cs.com.cn/zgzqb/images/2021-11/24/A20/zqA2024.pdf); reported Stanley-supplier link not verified so omitted.

name: Tan Bingwen
current_role: Director and major shareholder (~11%), Guangdong Shenling Environmental Systems (申菱环境, SZSE: 301018), Foshan
profile: Tan Bingwen is a long-standing shareholder and board director of Shenling Environment, a Shunde (Foshan) maker of specialty HVAC and thermal-management systems; chairman and controlling shareholder is Cui Yingqi. Shenling's data-services segment supplies liquid- and air-cooling (CDUs, manifolds, cold plates, precision air-con) to cloud and AI-compute data centres, plus energy-storage and grid cooling.
interesting_fact: Shenling began researching data-centre liquid cooling in 2011, built one of China's early commercial liquid-cooled micro-module data centres with China Mobile and Inspur, holds 72 liquid-cooling patents and was ranked No.1 CDU vendor in China's 2024 liquid-cooled data-centre market (CCID).
notes: Highly relevant to data-centre cooling topic. No personal bio found; he is a director, not chairman (2026 pay notice: https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202604261821589318_1.pdf). He filed to reduce holdings in late 2025. Chairman Cui Yingqi may be the better interview target; route via board secretary office.

name: Jin Xiaotuan
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Hangzhou Honghua Digital Technology / Atexco (宏华数科, SSE STAR: 688789)
profile: Born 1956, Jin Xiaotuan studied silk engineering at the Zhejiang Silk Institute of Technology and taught there in the 1980s, exploring digitalisation of textiles. He founded Honghua (Atexco), now a leading Chinese maker of industrial digital textile-printing machines and inks, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market. He holds ~24% directly and is actual controller.
interesting_fact: Atexco makes high-speed single-pass and multi-pass inkjet textile printers (Vega series) plus reactive, disperse and pigment inks, competing globally with European printer makers; Jin has spent roughly three decades focused solely on digital inkjet printing.
deep_cut_fact: His turning point came at the 1999 ITMA textile-machinery show in France, where he first encountered digital textile printing and resolved to bring the technology to China (Shanghai Securities News profile, Sept 2025).
notes: Board secretary is Yu Jianli (per 10jqka company page https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/688789/company.html). Web-search budget ran out before locating the IR email; check the latest SSE annual report summary. Cnstock source not directly fetched (503); facts from search summary.

name: Ray O'Rourke
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Laing O'Rourke (stepped back from the CEO role in July 2024)
profile: Raymond Gabriel O'Rourke (b. 1947, Co. Leitrim, Ireland) built R O'Rourke & Son into one of Britain's biggest private contractors, buying John Laing's construction arm in 2001 to form Laing O'Rourke, which he runs with his brother Des and majority-owns. The group builds infrastructure, rail, healthcare, energy and data-centre projects in the UK, Australia and the Middle East, known for off-site 'modern methods of construction'.
interesting_fact: He was made an Honorary Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire (KBE) in 2011 and holds honorary doctorates from Dublin Institute of Technology and Queen's University Belfast.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Corraleehan near Ballinamore, South Leitrim, he started out in London as a 'pony boy' carrying muck out from under the city while the Victoria Line was being built.
notes: Famously press-shy. Laing O'Rourke has a dedicated Data Centres and Energy & Water practice, relevant to the podcast. Route via UK press office.

name: Raymond Debbane
current_role: President & CEO, The Invus Group (New York) and CEO of Artal Group; director of Lexicon Pharmaceuticals; Invus is a 10%+ holder of Scholar Rock
profile: Lebanese-born investor Ray Debbane was a BCG manager in Paris before forming Invus in 1985. Backed by the European family group Artal with permanent ('continuous') capital, Invus has compounded to $10bn+ under management, taking long-horizon stakes in consumer and biotech companies such as Lexicon and Scholar Rock. His SEC-reported wealth reflects those holdings.
interesting_fact: Invus has no fund life or forced exit timetable: its capital comes solely from Artal, and the modest initial pool from 1985 has compounded to over $10bn even after distributing billions to Artal shareholders.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance he trained as a food scientist: a BS in agricultural sciences and agricultural engineering from the American University of Beirut and an MS in Food Science and Technology from UC Davis (then a Stanford MBA). He chairs Action Against Hunger USA.
notes: Also Trustee Emeritus of Connecticut College. Low media profile; Invus New York office is the published route.

name: Christopher R Gordon
current_role: Partner, Global Head of Private Equity and Global Head of Healthcare, Bain Capital (Boston); former Kestra Medical director (2021 to Sept 2025)
profile: Chris Gordon joined Bain Capital in 1997 after consulting at Bain & Company and now leads its global private equity and healthcare investing. He has sat on boards of HCA, Quintiles (IQVIA), Waystar, Surgery Partners, Stada and Kestra Medical (wearable defibrillators), which Bain controls via West Affum Holdings. The SEC-derived net worth likely reflects Bain-held Kestra shares attributed to him, not personal holdings.
interesting_fact: He has served on the boards of a who's-who of healthcare buyouts, including HCA, Quintiles Transnational (now IQVIA), Grupo NotreDame Intermedica and Cerevel Therapeutics.
deep_cut_fact: He was a Baker Scholar (top of class distinction) at Harvard Business School, graduated magna cum laude in economics from Harvard College, and is a founding Director of the Healthcare Private Equity Association.
notes: Net worth figure ($646M) is likely an artefact: Kestra proxy lists his address c/o Bain Capital and shows no personal beneficial ownership; the 10% stake belongs to Bain funds. He left Kestra's board Sept 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1877184/000119312526320956/ck0001877184-20260727.htm). Member, Council on Foreign Relations.

name: Yu Dong
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Bona Film Group (博纳影业, SZSE: 001330), Beijing
profile: Yu Dong (Don Yu, b. 1971, Beijing) graduated from the Beijing Film Academy, worked at Beijing Film Studio and ran domestic distribution at China Film Group before founding Bona in 1999. Bona became China's first private film distributor and a producer of 'new mainstream' blockbusters such as Operation Red Sea and The Battle at Lake Changjin. He now pushes AI-driven film production (Bona AIGMS centre).
interesting_fact: Bona's 'China Victory' trilogy includes The Battle at Lake Changjin, which became China's all-time box-office champion; Bona's films total 350+ titles and over 70bn yuan in box office.
deep_cut_fact: Bona was the first domestic private company to receive a film distribution licence from China's film regulator (1999); in 2005 Screen International dubbed it 'the Chinese Miramax'.
notes: Vice-chair of the China Film Association and president of the Hengdian Film Industry Association. Bona is investing heavily in AI film production, a possible podcast angle.

name: Li Shaobo
current_role: Founder, Chairman/legal representative and controlling shareholder, Sinocare Inc. (三诺生物, SZSE: 300298), Changsha
profile: Li Shaobo founded Sinocare in Changsha in 2002 to make affordable blood-glucose meters, taking it public in 2012 as China's first listed glucose-meter company. Sinocare is No.1 in China's glucose-meter market and claims No.4 worldwide after buying US-based Nipro Diagnostics (now Trividia Health) and PTS Diagnostics in 2016; it is expanding into continuous glucose monitoring and diabetes digital management.
interesting_fact: Sinocare says more than half of Chinese people with diabetes who self-monitor use its products, and it operates in 187 countries and regions with 9 R&D/manufacturing sites.
notes: Confirmed as company head and actual controller in the H1 2026 report. Personal background not verified (search budget exhausted).

name: Feng Huanpei
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Beijing Jingyuntong Technology Co., Ltd. (京运通, SSE: 601908)
profile: Feng Huanpei chairs and, with his holding vehicle Jingyuntong Daxing Technology Investment, controls Beijing Jingyuntong, a solar-industry group spanning crystal-growth furnaces and other high-end equipment, monocrystalline silicon production (bases in Wuhai, Leshan and Wuxi), PV/wind power plants, and environmental products such as denitration catalysts. Family wealth is shared with Fan Zhaoxia.
interesting_fact: Jingyuntong is one of the few Chinese solar players spanning the whole chain from building the crystal-growing furnaces, to pulling monocrystalline silicon, to owning and operating PV and wind power plants.
notes: Highly relevant energy/solar-manufacturing guest. Chairmanship confirmed in 2026 board notice (临2026-029). No personal bio verified; search budget exhausted.

name: Hu Jiqiang
current_role: Chairman of Conba Group (康恩贝集团, private holding company); former chairman of listed Zhejiang Conba Pharmaceutical (SSE: 600572), now under Zhejiang state-led mixed ownership. Current titles not freshly verified.
profile: Hu Jiqiang (b. 1961, Dongyang, Zhejiang) graduated in pharmacy from Zhejiang Medical University and built Conba into a major Chinese maker of traditional-Chinese and Western OTC/prescription medicines (brands such as Changyanning and Qianliekang). He served as a deputy to the 12th and 13th National People's Congress. After a mixed-ownership reform, Zhejiang provincial state capital became the listed company's controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Conba traces its roots to a beekeeping farm founded by a group of beekeepers in Lanxi, Zhejiang in 1969; today its Changyanning line alone brings in close to 1.3bn yuan a year.
notes: Bio source: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E8%83%A1%E5%AD%A3%E5%BC%BA. The listed company is now state-led (site links Zhejiang International Trade Group / Zhejiang TCM Health Industry Group), so the listed-company board office may not route to him; his own Conba Group holding is the more direct route.
